review_conclusions.finding: Full extraction bytes are written before validation and bound by byte count/hash, decoded count, exact forbidden codepoint counts and parser identity. The HTTP raw body/redirect chain remains archived. Invalid UTF-8 PDF stdout is retained as bytes and rejected explicitly. Rejected text never enters successful evidence or cache.

One Unicode-category Cc check covers PDF, decoded text and visible HTML; TAB LF CR FF VT NEL are allowed layout controls. U+001C–001F survive HTML whitespace normalization, preventing silent disappearance before detection. Hidden/script controls do not contaminate visible extraction. No stripping or repair occurs.

Cache keys include validation policy but remain independent of focus. Fresh consumers explicitly require that policy and reject receipt downgrade. Legacy receipts remain verifiable as historical transport, with not_recorded_by_legacy_policy; they do not establish current readability, and old cache keys cannot masquerade as current validated entries.

No task/site/domain lists, density threshold, count padding, source truncation, model/browser fallback, automatic retry or extra fetch loop. Explicit agent retries retain their existing behavior. Only page_fetch/repl_tools/archive_audit product sources changed; research root and its pinned formatter, refiner prompts/transports, models, deadlines, call budgets, scheduling, strict evaluators and pinned RLM sources are unchanged.

A single forbidden non-layout control rejects the entire extraction even when much surrounding text is readable. This is an explicit general acceptance policy change; it must not be described as unchanged research outcomes. All affected arms require the common-code replay already planned.

limitations: Category-Cc rejection is not a proof that every remaining printable glyph is correct, or that every visually rendered PDF/HTML source has complete semantically accurate extraction. Missing ToUnicode may also yield plausible but wrong printable symbols or empty output.

The rejected artifact retains exact extracted bytes. For HTML, ordinary pre-existing visible-text extraction/whitespace normalization remains; raw HTTP bytes preserve original markup and hidden material.
No OCR/browser/model repair fallback is added. No unqualified historical readable-size claim is authorized by receipt compatibility.

Independent actual corpus covered four affected Frozen1 artifacts and all49 clean B0-1 artifacts. Author separately tested KIAS as a fifth affected artifact; that result is not represented as an additional independent reviewer replay.
No broad full suite or new live experiment was run by this reviewer. Focused tests are bounded to changed behavior and prior direct-fetch/audit contracts.
